summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and biliary stents, was admitted with a fever of 101.2°F and night sweats, following a recent chemotherapy cycle. He had no localizing symptoms, and evaluation showed no evidence of infection. Chest X-ray revealed no acute process, and abdominal ultrasound showed stable biliary ductal dilation and gallbladder sludge without signs of obstruction. Liver enzymes were mildly elevated, but bilirubin remained normal. Blood cultures were negative at 48 hours, and he remained afebrile after initial presentation. Antibiotics were discontinued, and he was discharged home in stable condition with plans to continue outpatient oncology care.
